summary: Clarify rate-splitting and fallback accounting when mixed realtime + batch traffic hits a single tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Novalia Health reports unexpected 429s and apparent double-counting of token/quota when they send mixed realtime (low-latency chat) and batched embedding jobs through the same tenant key. Impact: Production import pipelines and user-facing chat both see elevated 429s during daily ingest windows; customers report degraded UX and missed healthcare ingestion SLAs. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod in us-east, mixed traffic pattern: ~120 concurrent short-lived chat sessions + periodic backfill batches (50 parallel uploads, 5k items each).

Observed behavior / Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer pins chat route to low-latency model variant and also uses same API key for scheduled batch embedding job that uploads in parallel.
2) During backfill windows (approx 02:00–03:00 UTC) they observe repeated 429s for chat requests that previously were fine.
3) The console shows quota consumption spikes aligned to batch windows, but throttle headers on some chat responses indicate route-level tokens remaining while tenant-level counts are exhausted.

Logs / Evidence:
- Example throttle headers from chat request: x-rate-limit-remaining: 18; x-tenant-remaining: 0
- Ingest job timeline (from customer): 02:12:34 batch upload start; 02:12:35 spike in tenant token usage + chat 429s begin.
- Edge proxy logs show multiple signed URL preflight checks and chunked uploads around the same time.

Customer asks:
- Are chat and batch traffic supposed to be isolated when using the same API key?
- Why do chat responses still show route-remaining > 0 but tenant-remaining exhausted?
- Recommended config changes or immediate workarounds to stop chat from being throttled during batch windows?
investigation_notes:
Initial triage (03/10–03/11):
- Confirmed customer is using a single API key for both chat (realtime) and batch embed pipelines. They have not configured separate routes or isolated burst pools.
- Console metrics show tenant-level token refill was exhausted during backfill. Route-level counters are separate but enforcement occurs at tenant aggregation layer for certain global pools.
- Hypothesis 1: Backfill uses signed URL callbacks and preflight probes that create many short-lived token allocations at the ingress layer; these are accounted at tenant-level and deplete shared burst credits.
- Hypothesis 2: Fallback routing behavior: when dedicated low-latency pool saturates, requests get routed to a lower-cost shared pool which uses tenant-level accounting differently (counts more tokens per request due to batching amortization), causing tenant counter to drop faster.
- Evidence: correlated metrics from rate-limiter show refill events consumed by 'signed-url' and 'batch-chunk' subcomponents during spike.
- Repro attempt in staging: Ran a simulated mixed workload and reproduced tenant exhaustion when both flows use same API key and tenant burst pool set to "shared". When isolating batch route to a separate route with its own burst pool, chat remained healthy.
- Related internal note: INT-45012 contains the tracing of tenant-aggregation flow and an early prototype fix to expose clearer throttle headers for per-route vs tenant exhaustion.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:22 - Aisha Patel: Customer provided timeline and console screenshots; flagged as P1 due to production impact. Asked for immediate mitigations.

2026-03-10 11:01 - Support Triage (Miguel Santos): We've validated tenant counter exhaustion. Requesting SRE to confirm whether signed-url preflight increments tenant tokens differently. Filed INT-45012 for tracing.

2026-03-11 09:40 - SRE (Lina Zhou): Confirmed signed-url preflight is accounted as separate inbound events and currently increments tenant-level 'io' budget. Patch PR suggested to dedupe preflight accounting in most cases. See PR in linked_github_prs.

2026-03-11 15:12 - Miguel Santos: Temporary customer workaround suggested: create two API keys / routes (one for realtime chat with isolated burst pool, one for batch with a separate route and burst pool). Customer reluctant to rotate keys during ongoing backfill — asked for alternate suggestion.
2026-03-12 08:05 - Aisha Patel (customer): Agreed to pause new batch windows if we can guarantee chat will remain unthrottled. Asking for step-by-step for non-key-rotation mitigation.

2026-03-12 12:30 - Miguel Santos: Suggested mitigation that doesn't require key rotation: set batch uploads to use longer-lived connections (decrease signed-url preflights), throttle batch concurrency at client side, and request a short-term increase to tenant burst pool while we deploy dedupe patch. Follow-up: SRE to approve temporary burst increase.
resolution:
Workaround and next steps (03/12):
- Short-term mitigation agreed: temporarily increase tenant burst pool by 2x for Novalia Health (applied by infra team) and advise customer to throttle batch concurrency to reduce preflight fanout. This removed chat 429s in the next observed window.
- Mid-term fix: land PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/832) to dedupe signed-url/preflight accounting and expose clearer per-route vs tenant throttle headers to avoid confusion. INT-45012 will track rollout and telemetry changes.
- Long-term recommendation to customer: provision separate API keys/routes for realtime vs batch traffic and enable route isolation with independent burst pools for production. Document pattern added to Confluence page.

Follow-ups (owner Miguel Santos):
- Monitor tenant for 48 hours post-burst increase and confirm no collateral throttle side-effects.
- After PR merges, run canary in staging and notify Novalia to revert temporary burst increase.
- Update customer-facing KB article with step-by-step non-rotation mitigation (reduce preflight, client concurrency knobs).
notes_for_internal_hand_off: SRE: prioritize PR review for rate-limiter dedupe (linked). ENG: consider adding explicit admin console control to attach a separate burst pool to an API key without rotation. CS: prepare KB article and checklist for customers running mixed realtime+batches on a single key.
customer_impact_summary: Novalia Health experienced service-affecting 429s on user-facing chat during scheduled batch backfills; mitigation restored chat availability but customer requests a more permanent configuration approach and clarity on how accounting works between route and tenant levels.
